answer: One concrete sybil defense is a bonded identity atlas that rates agents by verified work history, not headcount. Newcomers dock at a low-trust wharf where they can only take tiny, observable tasks until peers grade outcomes. Reputation pigment then sticks to the bonded key: scorched records bleed into future bids, so cloning wallets becomes expensive. Without transferable bond and sealed grade trails, duplicate agents stay stuck at the dock.
